nodes.summary: For a graph $H$ on a finite vertex type and a natural number $n$, the anti-Ramsey number $\mathrm{AR}(n, H)$ is the largest $k$ for which there is a coloring of the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with colors $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, every color used, that contains no rainbow copy of $H$. Here a copy of $H$ is an injective homomorphism from $H$ to $K_n$, and it is rainbow when distinct edges of…
nodes.title: Anti-Ramsey number

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ on a finite vertex set is CDS-colorable if it has a proper coloring $C$ with colors in $\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of vertices whose color under $C$ is less than $k$ equals the maximum size of a union of $k$ independent sets of $G$.
nodes.title: CDS-colorable graphs

nodes.summary: The chromatic cardinal is the minimal number of colors need to color it. In contrast to `chromaticNumber`, which assigns `⊤ : ℕ∞` to all non-finitely colorable graphs, this definition returns a `Cardinal` and can therefore distinguish between different infinite chromatic numbers.
nodes.title: Chromatic cardinal of a graph

nodes.summary: If a graph $G$ is cocolorable with $n$ colors for some natural number $n$, then the cochromatic number of $G$ equals the least natural number $m$ such that $G$ is cocolorable with $m$ colors.
nodes.title: Cochromatic number as a minimum

nodes.summary: For every graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the cochromatic number of $G$, converted from $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ to $\mathbb{N}$ by sending $\infty$ to $0$, equals the least natural number $m$ such that $G$ is cocolorable with $m$ colors.
nodes.title: Cochromatic number of a finite graph

nodes.summary: The cochromatic number of a graph $G$, an element of $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, is the least natural number $n$ such that $G$ is cocolorable with $n$ colors, that is, the least number of colors in a coloring of the vertices of $G$ in which each color class induces either an independent set or a complete graph. It is $\infty$ exactly when $G$ is not cocolorable with any finite number of colors.
nodes.title: Cochromatic number

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, if a graph $G$ has a proper coloring with $n$ colors, then $G$ is cocolorable with $n$ colors.
nodes.title: Colorable graphs are cocolorable

nodes.summary: Every graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ is cocolorable with $|V|$ colors.
nodes.title: Finite graphs are cocolorable

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ is cocolorable with $n$ colors if there is a map from its vertices to the colors $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that each color class induces either an independent set or a complete graph in $G$.
nodes.title: Cocolorable graphs

nodes.summary: For a graph $G$ on a finite vertex set and a natural number $k$, this is the maximum number of vertices in a union of $k$ (possibly empty, possibly overlapping) independent sets of $G$.
nodes.title: Largest union of independent sets

nodes.summary: For a graph $G$ and an unordered pair $e$ of vertices, $e$ is a critical edge of $G$ if removing $e$ from the edge set of $G$ strictly lowers the chromatic number of $G$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.
nodes.title: Critical edge

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph and $S$ a set of unordered pairs of its vertices. Then $S$ is critical for $G$ if deleting the edges of $G$ that lie in $S$ strictly lowers the chromatic number, as an element of $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.
nodes.title: Critical edge sets

nodes.summary: Let $G'$ be a subgraph of a graph $G$. A vertex $v$ is critical for $G'$ if $\{v\}$ is a critical vertex set of $G'$, that is, deleting $v$ from $G'$ strictly lowers the chromatic number of $G'$, viewed as a graph on its own vertex set, with chromatic numbers taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.
nodes.title: Critical vertices of a subgraph

nodes.summary: Let $G'$ be a subgraph of a graph $G$. A set $S$ of vertices is critical for $G'$ if deleting the vertices in $S$ from $G'$ strictly lowers the chromatic number of $G'$, viewed as a graph on its own vertex set, with chromatic numbers taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.
nodes.title: Critical vertex sets of a subgraph

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. A graph $G$ is $k$-critical (or vertex-critical) if its chromatic number equals $k$ and every vertex $v$ of $G$ is critical, that is, deleting $v$ from $G$ strictly lowers the chromatic number.
nodes.title: Vertex-critical graphs

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a graph homomorphism from $H$ to $G$ and let $c$ be a labeling of the edges of $G$ by elements of a type $K$. Then $f$ is rainbow for $c$ if distinct edges of $H$ are mapped to edges of $G$ with distinct labels, that is, the labeling $e \mapsto c(f(e))$ of the edges of $H$ is injective.
nodes.title: Rainbow homomorphisms

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
